Arkansas has introduced no AI-related legislation as of August 2026, making it one of the states where the regulatory environment for AI development and deployment remains entirely unaddressed at the statutory level.

The absence of bills means there is no state-level framework governing how AI systems are built, sold, or used within Arkansas. This is a fact about legislative inaction, not about the absence of AI activity in the state. The data does not indicate whether federal rules, executive orders, or local ordinances fill that gap.

Nothing in this data connects to compute infrastructure, power capacity, or data center development in Arkansas. Those conditions may or may not exist, but this dataset does not cover them.
